name: Accountant multi-client Companies House filing console
demand: The core trigger survives: Companies House confirmed on 23 October 2026 that from April 2028 all UK registered companies, including those filing through accountants, must submit accounts in iXBRL using commercial software; web and paper accounts filing will close. That same-day update paused the small-company and micro-entity profit-and-loss filing change, retaining abridged and filleted accounts, so the software mandate remains but the extra-disclosure scope is smaller than previously announced: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/companies-house-update-to-accounts-filing-from-april-2028. Companies House’s accounts-data page, last updated 10 October 2026, says it expects 2.2 million accounts annually and that about 75% are currently filed electronically: https://download.companieshouse.gov.uk/en_monthlyaccountsdata.html. Companies House reported 5.48 million companies on the register at 31 March 2026; that is an upper-bound population, not the number of active clients or accountant-managed accounts: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/companies-house-annual-report-and-accounts-2025-to-2026/companies-house-annual-report-and-accounts-2025-to-2026. A private Companies House-data count found 49,124 active incorporated firms with accounting, bookkeeping or tax as their primary SIC code in its 1 August 2026 snapshot; it excludes unincorporated practices and notes that SIC codes are self-selected: https://practicegroup.co.uk/insights/how-many-accountancy-firms-uk/. TaxCalc’s current marketing site reports 12,000+ UK practices using its products and 400,000+ accounts filed in FY2024–25; these are vendor-reported figures, and the filing count is historical, not independent evidence of current demand: https://www.taxcalc.com/about and https://www.taxcalc.com/products/tax-and-accounts. Search volumes and app-install counts: unverified.
prices: Published list prices show an established, low-cost market: TaxCalc Accounts Production is £164/year for 12 clients, £368 for 50, £744 for 150 and £1,050 for 1,000, excluding VAT: https://shop.taxcalc.com/accountancy-software-prices. Andica Cloud Accounts Production starts at £100/year excluding VAT: https://www.andica.com/andica-accounts-production-software-cloud-pricing.html. Capium’s small suite starts at £140/month excluding VAT for up to 100 clients; its pricing page also lists Accounts Production as a £20/month small-band module, so confirm which configuration applies: https://www.capium.com/pricing/. Forbes Accounts is £335/year plus VAT: https://www.tax.co.uk/products_accounts.html. IRIS Elements Accounts Production lists £125.18 per user/year plus a client-band subscription, with a 10-client minimum: https://www.iris.co.uk/products/iris-elements/accounts-production/. A direct recent comparator, AccountsGear, lists £35/month for up to 10 clients: https://accountsgear.co.uk/. These are asking prices, not verified transactions or realized revenue.

revenue_proof.claim: ZERO WEIGHT under the requested age rule: Acorah Software Products Limited, the company behind the TaxCalc trading name, reported £15,163,936 turnover for the year ending 31 March 2025. This is company-wide turnover, not accounts-production revenue; the underlying period ended more than 18 months before 23 October 2026. The accounts were filed on 18 August 2025. Sources: https://www.192.com/atoz/financial/business/03948264/, https://www.taxcalc.com/legal-disclaimer, https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/03948264/filing-history. No recent product-specific revenue or paid-customer evidence was verified.

copy_speed: High. AccountsGear is a direct product overlap: its current site describes trial-balance-to-accounts, iXBRL, approval and filing, at £35/month for up to 10 clients. Its blog has dated posts from July to September 2026, but an exact product launch date is unverified; its own page says its evidence review used a fictional test portfolio, so customer traction is also unverified: https://accountsgear.co.uk/ and https://accountsgear.co.uk/blog. Recent adjacent launches show fast incumbent iteration: IRIS Firm Management launched 12 May 2026 for practice workflows, not accounts production: https://www.iris.co.uk/news/iris-launches-practice-management-platform-ifm-uk/. Andica released a new Charity Accounts product on 13 May 2026: https://andica.com/news.html. Sage launched Period Review on 15 September 2026 for multi-client MTD transaction review, not year-end accounts production: https://www.sage.com/en-gb/company/digital-newsroom/2026/09/sage-unveils-period-review-to-help-accountants-and-bookkeepers-manage-growing-mtd-workload/. Xero announced a new limited-company accounts-production experience on 26 March 2026, just before the requested April cutoff: https://blog.xero.com/uk/product-updates/streamlined-accounts-production/. TaxCalc already offers a batch filer for multiple approved submissions: https://www.taxcalc.com/products/tax-and-accounts.
platform_risk: High dependence on Companies House filing access, accepted iXBRL formats and changing taxonomies: Companies House says commercial software files through its XML gateway, and its guidance records taxonomy changes and retirements: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/using-software-to-file-your-companys-information. The Companies House REST API Filing documentation lists data-change services; it does not list accounts filing among those API products, so the specific future accounts-filing integration path should be verified with Companies House before building around it: https://developer-specs.company-information.service.gov.uk/ and https://developer-specs.company-information.service.gov.uk/manipulate-company-data-api-filing/guides/overview. Companies House says its software finder is a guide and does not endorse products: https://www.gov.uk/software-company-accounts. Public company data and electronically filed accounts data are downloadable free, weakening a data-access moat: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/companies-house-data-products and https://download.companieshouse.gov.uk/en_monthlyaccountsdata.html. No exclusive software or platform partner requirement was found in the reviewed sources.
defensible_asset: Weak if the product is mainly a filing UI or rules database: Companies House makes company information and filed accounts data available free, while taxonomy and filing requirements are publicly documented and updated: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/companies-house-data-products and https://www.gov.uk/guidance/using-software-to-file-your-companys-information. A plausible asset would have to accumulate through customer-specific trial-balance mappings, tested exception and validation rules, audit history, and integrations that embed the console in a practice’s workflow. Those assets are hypotheses, not evidence of an existing moat; client data would require appropriate permissions and controls.
build_effort: Very high for a complete preparation-and-filing engine; moderate for a narrow workflow layer on top of established accounts software. The full product must handle account preparation, UK reporting formats, iXBRL tagging, validation and rejected filings, client credentials, audit trail and data imports. Existing products already cover much of this scope, including IRIS’s tagged accounts, error reports, imports and direct submission: https://www.iris.co.uk/products/iris-elements/accounts-production/ and https://www.iris.co.uk/products/iris-accounts-production/. An agent-run solo build duration is unverified. The lower-effort wedge is a multi-client exception and readiness queue that exports into a client’s existing filing product, rather than replacing its accounts engine.
channel: Use inbound, product-branded acquisition: search content on the April 2028 transition, a public demo and opt-in trial, and discoverability through the Companies House software finder once the product qualifies; the finder is a directory, not an endorsement: https://www.gov.uk/software-company-accounts. Avoid unsolicited email, texts, WhatsApp and social DMs to sole traders or individuals: ICO guidance treats sole traders as individual subscribers and social DMs as electronic mail; consent or the soft opt-in is generally required for electronic marketing to them. The ICO distinguishes corporate subscribers, but this lead can rely on opt-in channels and avoid cold messaging altogether: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; the <=5-hour/week ceiling is not evidenced for this unbuilt product. Treat it as a post-launch acceptance gate after self-service onboarding, billing, routine support and monitoring are automated. Customer accountants would still review and approve filings in the existing market’s workflows: https://www.iris.co.uk/products/iris-accounts-production/ and https://accounts-os.com/about.
desk_test: Free, one-day, no-code test: make a clickable mock-up of a multi-client readiness and exception queue; compare it feature-by-feature with TaxCalc Batch Filer, IRIS, Capium and the live AccountsGear offer; then post a transparent opt-in request for practice feedback on a public professional channel whose rules allow it. Ask respondents to describe one recurring portfolio-wide task their current product fails to cover, name their current accounts software and state whether they would commit to a paid pilot at a price they consider worthwhile. Do not use cold DMs or infer demand from page views. The test can reveal a specific gap; paid demand remains unverified.
red_flags: Conditional survive, not a validated opportunity. The 2028 commercial-software/iXBRL mandate remains, but the 23 October 2026 pause removes the planned small-company and micro-entity P&L filing change: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/companies-house-update-to-accounts-filing-from-april-2028. The broad feature set is already sold by incumbents, and TaxCalc already supports batch filing: https://www.taxcalc.com/products/tax-and-accounts. AccountsGear is a direct recent competitor, though its launch date, customers and revenue are unverified: https://accountsgear.co.uk/. Accountant-specific unmet need and willingness to pay remain unverified. The numeric automation value 0 means no realized automation has been evidenced for this not-yet-built business; the >=50% target is unverified.
